summary: Describes NETBUGGER3, a third-level program from UCLA for debugging network programs and trying out protocols. The authors needed a stand-in for a remote system that would not be up for months, and realized many sites had the same problem.

plainLanguage.summary: NETBUGGER3 helps developers test network programs when the other computer is not ready. It can simulate a service, display exchanged data and later inspect traffic between two real systems.

subtitle: A network tool for testing protocols when a remote server is unavailable.

tldr.problem: UCLA needed to test a file-transfer program before the remote system it would communicate with was available.
tldr.mechanism: NETBUGGER3 lets a user issue NCP commands, inspect connections and exchange data while simulating or mediating a third-level protocol.
tldr.outcome: Other network hosts could arrange to use it to debug programs or inspect messages between a client and a real server.

today: RFC 162 describes a network debugging program in May 1971. The unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: Why NETBUGGER3 Was Written
sections.content:
UCLA was writing an RJE FILENET program to interact with UCLA-CCN, but that system would not be available for several months. The author needed a way to simulate CCN and realized other network sites faced similar delays when their intended servers were not running.

NETBUGGER3 is described as a third-level program for debugging second- and third-level programs and experimenting with or simulating third-level protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: A program can be hard to test if the computer it needs is not running yet. NETBUGGER3 provides a way to test against a simulated service instead of waiting.

sections.title: Commands and Data Inspection
sections.content:
A user can issue RTS, STR and LISTEN commands, check connection status, receive and display NCP-USER events, and send or receive data over as many as twelve connections per running copy. Data can be displayed or entered as ASCII, EBCDIC or hexadecimal.

NETBUGGER3 can act as the initiator, receiver or an intermediate party in connections.
sections.plainLanguage: NETBUGGER3 can open and monitor connections, and users can inspect or enter data in several encodings. It can take different roles in a connection.

sections.title: Testing at Other Sites
sections.content:
A host developing a special third-level protocol could arrange with UCLA to interact with NETBUGGER3 while its intended server was unavailable. Alternatively, a user could log in to the UCLA system with Telnet and run the debugger on one console while running the program under test on another.

After the real server became available, NETBUGGER3 could act as an intermediary. The user could view, examine and, if needed, edit messages passing between the host and server.
sections.plainLanguage: Other sites could use UCLA's program before their intended server was ready. Later, it could sit between real systems so a developer could examine their messages.
